explanation: Breadth-first search the starting cell’s same-color component. Flip a cell when it is enqueued so it cannot be enqueued twice, and explore only horizontal and vertical neighbors of its original color.
timeComplexity: O(rows × columns). Each component cell is flipped before enqueueing and considers four neighbors, preventing duplicate enqueues.
spaceComplexity: O(rows × columns). The queue contains cells from the component; JavaScript retains its consumed queue entries until the call ends.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/matrix_connected_regions.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Only cells matching the starting original color are enqueued, and each is flipped before enqueuing. That flip marks it visited, so no cell is processed twice. Four-neighbor expansion reaches exactly the starting component and changes no differently colored or disconnected cell.
walkthrough: For start (0,0) in [[1,1,0],[0,1,0],[1,0,0]], the connected 1 cells are (0,0),(0,1),(1,1). Flipping them gives [[0,0,0],[0,0,0],[1,0,0]]; the isolated 1 at (2,0) remains. JSON arguments are [row,column,image], not [image,row,column]. The observed output is the mutated image; native Boolean image types are converted by their wrappers.
edgeCases: Diagonal contact alone does not connect cells.
An isolated starting pixel is still flipped.
The starting value determines the component before any recoloring.
